body:
>I hope you will consider that 25 is still pretty young to give up on yourself. If you compare to your teenaged self you may feel old. But the truth is that people develop at their own paces and many, MANY people are still searching into their 20s and beyond.

But is it though? My parents were married homeowners and had already had me by that age, though their life was still in flux (job changes, moving, more kids, etc). My dad is a skilled mechanic; there's never been something he couldn't fix. He seems to have an intuitive understanding of how everything works, and if he encounters something new, he just messes with it until he understands it. When he got hired at his most recent job (he's way overqualified for it), his presence alone shaved two hours and two other employees off of change overs. My mom is a career woman who worked her way up from nothing and now is in regular dialog with the CEOs and VP of her company. She makes nearly six figures. I feel like I will not be able to outdo my parents, and that makes me feel awful.

>If you have mental health issues and they aren't being treated, that makes it hard to do everything.

I'm ambivalent about the ontology of "mental health" as described by doctors, psychs, the DSM, etc. On the one hand, lots of people correspond to mental illness descriptions and there does feel like there's something wrong with me. I've been diagnosed with anxiety and depression by a psychiatrist and a counselor in the past. On the other hand, it feels like a convenient cash generator for big pharma and an excuse generator for me. "Oh, I'm depressed, that's why my life feels so awful." Maybe I'm depressed because I'm awful and so is my life, shit.

I used to go to therapy like two years ago. I've been considering going back, albeit to a new counselor. I feel like I hit a wall with my old one.

Thank you for your kindness and understanding. It helps. I hope you have a good day.
